subject: Quantify required headroom for Q4 enterprise commit — SLA & tokens/sec mapping
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari.patel@veridocs.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Veridocs peak profile and target SLOs

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — quick follow up on the traffic profile so we can lock sizing for the PoC -> reserved capacity ask. High level:
- Expected peak concurrent users: ~1,200 (during heavy ingestion windows)
- Expected peak requests per second (RPS): 220–270 (95th percentile burst to account for batch upload spikes)
- Average generation per request: ~280 tokens (mix of extraction + short summarization)
- Target latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 1s; p99 <= 2s (end-to-end user-facing)
- Typical request pattern: 60% short (<400 tokens) single-shot, 40% multi-turn (average of 3 calls/session)

Can you map that to tokens/sec and give a recommended dedicated footprint + suggested headroom for a 12-month reserved commitment? Also provide any quick mitigations if we need to hit the p95 target without over-committing GPUs.

Attached: veridocs_initial_profile.csv (summary) — will attach final procurement contacts next thread.

—Ari
Product & Ops, Veridocs AI
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@veridocs.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Veridocs peak profile and target SLOs

Ari — thanks, this is a helpful profile. Quick read-through below and an initial ballpark so procurement has something to react to. Detailed calc and spreadsheet attached (veridocs_throughput_model_v2.xlsx).

Summary of assumptions I'm using for the model:
- Working model: quantized 70B conversational variant (latency-focused profile), comparable to our "rtd-70b-q" runtime.
- Per-GPU sustained throughput (p95-optimized, with our continuous batching + KV cache): ~5k tokens/sec per A100-class GPU for this workload mix. This is an internal conservative estimate accounting for multi-turn KV growth.
- Request mix -> tokens/sec baseline calc: 250 RPS * 280 tokens = 70,000 tokens/sec baseline.
- SLO headroom target: 30% baseline headroom (to cover sudden bursts, token distribution skew, and model warmup), so target capacity = 91,000 tokens/sec.

Initial capacity recommendation (baseline -> reserved commit):
- Capacity units required (no headroom): 70,000 / 5,000 = 14 GPUs
- Capacity units with 30% headroom: 91,000 / 5,000 = 18.2 -> recommend 19 GPUs reserved

Mitigations to reduce committed footprint / cost:
- Increase KV prefix caching for known invitation templates (reduces per-request tokens for ~20% of requests) -> effective tokens/sec drop of ~6–8%
- Use burst-on-demand pool for 3–4 GPUs to handle p99 spikes rather than reserving full headroom (saves ~20% committed spend)
- Consider shifting 25% of multi-turn workload to a smaller model for read-only summarization paths (requires application routing but can cut committed GPUs by 2–3)

I'll ask Karthik for a tighter hardware-profile calc (tokens/sec per GPU for p95/p99) and an SLO-fit table (p95/p99 vs GPU count) before we formalize the 12-month commit ask.

Next: Karthik — can you drop a short table for p95/p99 tokens/sec per GPU and an alternate plan if the customer insists on p95 <= 800ms?

Thanks,
Sofia
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Ari Patel <ari.patel@veridocs.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Veridocs peak profile and target SLOs

On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 11:03 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com> wrote:
> Next: Karthik — can you drop a short table for p95/p99 tokens/sec per GPU and an alternate plan if the customer insists on p95 <= 800ms?

Quick technical breakdown (short, actionable):
Assumptions: quantized 70B, steady-state with continuous batching, typical sequence lengths per Ari's mix. Numbers are tuned for our current kernel set and include modest overhead for KV growth.

Per-GPU effective throughput (tokens/sec):
- p95 throughput: 5,000 tokens/sec (conservative; aligns w/ Sofia)
- p99 throughput: 3,800 tokens/sec (accounts for tail and increased memory pressure)
- p50 (best-effort batching): 6,800 tokens/sec

SLO fit table (target tokens/sec -> GPUs required):
- Baseline tokens/sec (70,000): p95 -> 14 GPUs; p99 -> 19 GPUs
- With 30% headroom (91,000): p95 -> 19 GPUs; p99 -> 24 GPUs

If customer needs p95 <= 800ms (more aggressive):
- Options: increase dedicated GPUs to move off the p95 curve (recommended 25 GPUs reserved), or
- Add an accelerator tier (smaller model for first-pass + short-circuit caching) to reduce average tokens/generation by ~20% and hit p95 w/ ~19 GPUs, or
- Hybrid: reserve 16 GPUs for baseline + 8 GPUs in burst-on-demand (keeps reservation cost down but guarantees p99 via burst pool).

Operational notes / recommended guardrails for procurement doc:
- SLA-backed reserved pool should include automatic fallback rules to a slightly cheaper model variant if capacity is exhausted (ensures availability).
- Plan for a 6-week ramp post-commit where we profile actual tokens/sec and adjust autoscaling thresholds.

I attached a candidate pricing/footprint sheet to the internal draft. If Ari/Procurement are comfortable with the hybrid, we can propose 19 reserved + 6 burst-on-demand for the 12-month term. That yields a practical p95 fit and a p99 mitigation path.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Desai <samir@veridocs.ai>

Subject: Re: Veridocs peak profile and target SLOs

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. A few quick items from procurement:
1) Can you provide the committed monthly invoice for 19 GPUs (12-month) and the incremental per-GPU burst rate?
2) We need the SLA proposal as a PDF to circulate (please include guaranteed p95 latency band and ramp clauses).
3) Are there simple service-level emulators we can run during the 6-week ramp to validate our traffic shape?

We are inclined to try the hybrid plan (19 reserved + 6 burst) but want to see the numbers for worst-case p99 exposure and the cost delta if we move to 24 reserved (procurement asks for the delta so they can weigh predictability vs unit cost).

Attaching procurement contact info and the initial traffic CSV. If you can get the pricing and SLA PDF by EOD Tuesday we can put this on the Oct 7 procurement call.

Appreciate it — Samir
Head of Platform, Veridocs AI
